name: default_triage
description: Default fast-triage scoring configuration for the Adaptive Discovery Orchestrator. Uses MolScore's descriptor and filter functions to aggressively discard non-viable molecules.

desc_MolWt.reason: Lead-like MW window 250-450. Lower bound rejects fragments that dock well per-atom but are not leads; upper bound (tightened from Lipinski's 500) leaves headroom for lead-optimisation growth.

desc_NumHeavyAtoms.reason: Lead-like heavy-atom window 18-35. The lower bound is the key fragment filter: rigid small aromatics (biphenyl ~12, naphthalene ~10) score deceptively well in Vina because affinity scales with size. A generator that under-produces size will mostly fail this — that is the intended signal, not a bug.

desc_SAScore.reason: Synthetic Accessibility <= 4.5 (tightened from 5.0 to discard hard-to-synthesise scaffolds)

desc_QED.reason: QED Drug-likeness >= 0.5 (tightened from 0.3; first-pass Phase 1 guess, re-calibrated against expert input in Phase 2)

filter_ChemicalSanity.reason: No non-physical / unstable substructures. Catches the chemically dubious graphs (allenes, ketenes, strained heteroatom rings) that generative models emit and that RDKit sanitisation alone lets through.

chemical_sanity_smarts.name: cumulated_double_bonds
chemical_sanity_smarts.reason: Allene / cumulene — almost never a viable drug substructure when emitted by a generator.

chemical_sanity_smarts.name: triple_bond_in_ring
chemical_sanity_smarts.reason: Triple bond inside a ring — non-physical for ordinary ring sizes.

chemical_sanity_smarts.name: all_heteroatom_three_ring
chemical_sanity_smarts.reason: Three-membered ring of all heteroatoms — unstable.
